Sundar Pichai became CEO of Google in 2015 and CEO of Alphabet in 2019. He has held roles such as vice president of product development, senior vice president, and product chief.

**Sundar Pichai** is an Indian-born American executive who was [CEO](https://britannica.com/money/chief-executive-officer) of both [Google, Inc.](https://britannica.com/money/Google-Inc) (2015– ), and its [holding company](https://britannica.com/money/holding-company), [Alphabet, Inc.](https://britannica.com/money/Alphabet-Inc) (2019– ).

In 2011 Pichai reportedly was aggressively pursued for employment by microblogging service [Twitter](https://britannica.com/money/Twitter), and in 2014 he was touted as a possible CEO for [Microsoft](https://britannica.com/money/Microsoft-Corporation), but in both instances he was granted large financial packages to remain with Google. He also was known to have helped negotiate Google’s $3.2 billion deal to acquire Nest Labs in 2014. GOOGLE chief executive Sundar Pichai will assume the CEO role at parent firm Alphabet in a shakeup at the top of the Silicon Valley titan, the company said Tuesday.
Pichai will take over from Larry Page, a co-founder of the internet giant, at the holding firm which includes Google as well as units focusing on “other bets” in areas including self-driving cars and life sciences.

The 47-year-old Pichai, born in India, takes the helm at a time when Page and Brin have been noticeably absent and the company faces a torrent of controversies relating to its dominant position in the tech world.
Pichai is likely to fill a void at the company as it faces antitrust investigations and controversies over privacy and data practices in the United States and elsewhere.
